carbon_policy_signal.item: EPA scraps US power-plant climate rules, weakening global decarbonization narrative; EU policy response and MSR intake review expected by month-end.
carbon_policy_signal.why_it_matters: US climate rollback reduces scarcity premium on global emissions allowances; EU may reassess MSR intake and free-allocation strategy, creating downside pressure on EUA supply expectations and price floor.

freshness_caveat: Coal (26 Dec, 264 days stale) and Clean Dark (31 Dec, 259 days stale) — thermal merit-order signals unreliable; TTF, EUA, GB/DE power, storage, renewables current as of 15–16 Sept.
risk_flags: Coal data stale (26 Dec, 264 days old); clean_dark stale (31 Dec, 259 days old) — thermal merit-order signals unreliable.
Storage 16.1pp below 5-yr seasonal at 68.49% full; daily builds slowing (0.28% MTD) — refill pace critical for Oct–Mar thermal risk.
EUA −3.23% on EPA rollback; scarcity narrative deflates if global decarbonization slows — watch for further policy contagion.
Houthi Red Sea seizure raises LNG shipping 2–4 weeks; Corpus Christi Stage 3 ramp offsets — net TTF pressure unclear without flow data.

base.summary: TTF holds 77–80 EUR/MWh on Corpus Christi ramp offsetting Houthi delays; EUA stabilizes on policy reassessment.

downside.summary: Corpus Christi Stage 3 ramps faster; LNG arb to Europe widens; Red Sea corridor clears or rerouting becomes routine.

upside.summary: Houthi Red Sea escalation diverts LNG fleets; shipping delays extend 3–4 weeks; Corpus Christi ramp slips.

themes: Geopolitical LNG supply tightness vs. Corpus Christi ramp
Coal historically compressed; thermal dispatch risk on storage deficit
EUA policy shock: US climate reversal weakens scarcity narrative
GB power crash (-15.4% daily) vs. elevated DE (85th pctile, +28.5% MTD)
top_drivers: Houthi Red Sea control threatens LNG transit timing to NW Europe; geopolitical risk premium on TTF unless Corpus Christi Stage 3 ramp compensates.
EPA scraps US power-plant climate curbs (14 Sept); weakens global decarbonization momentum and deflates EUA scarcity narrative (−3.2σ sell-off).
Coal at 7th-percentile and storage 16pp below seasonal drive extended thermal call for winter; refill pace through Oct is key risk lever.
top_takeaway: Coal at 7th-percentile amid Houthi Red Sea threat tightens LNG/TTF; EUA crashes 3.2σ on EPA climate rollback; storage 16pp below seasonal keeps winter thermal call extended.

watchlist.why: Shipping delays and rerouting costs push Europe to compete harder for Atlantic supply; TTF upside unless Corpus Christi ramp absorbs outflow.
7th US LNG train online; early cargoes over next 4 weeks set the marginal cost floor for Atlantic LNG and EU gas spreads.
16pp seasonal deficit and slowing daily builds (0.28% MTD) tighten winter thermal call; Oct–Nov weather and Russian flows will set H2 power merit order.
US EPA climate scrub aired 14 Sept; watch for EU/UK policy response and MSR intake adjustments by month-end.
GB crashed −15.4% today (89th pctile) vs. DE +1.16% (85th pctile); wind/hydro intraday strength in GB may be temporary.
